findings.summary: When a modal opens for field errors without an error summary, focus goes to the first form control rather than the first invalid field, so users may miss the validation problem.
findings.fix: When opening after validation errors, focus the first [aria-invalid="true"] control; use the summary when present, and fall back to the first form control only when there are no field errors.
findings.evidence: data-modal-open-on-load is true for fieldErrors, but showFormDialog focuses the first input, select, or textarea.

findings.summary: The performance-review Teacher error is rendered without an ID or a programmatic relationship to its select, so assistive technology may not associate the error with the field.
findings.fix: Give the error paragraph a stable ID and conditionally reference it from the select with aria-describedby; set aria-invalid="true" while the error is present.
findings.evidence: The teacher select has no error-state attributes, and its conditional error paragraph has no ID.

findings.summary: Department and review-rating selects can describe a server-side error but do not expose the invalid state, leaving their error status unavailable as an ARIA state.
findings.fix: Conditionally add aria-invalid="true" to each select when its field error is present; retain the existing aria-describedby reference to the error text.
findings.evidence: Department and rating selects conditionally reference error text but never set aria-invalid.

passed: The modal component creates native dialog elements and names them with aria-labelledby references to their visible headings.
Modal triggers have aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-controls references to the generated dialog IDs.
Error summaries use role="alert" and are moved into an auto-opened dialog; success notices use role="status".
